dedupe_keys.name: food demand meta elasticities fdme database income and price elasticities from 215 studies with projections to 2050

description: The Food Demand Meta-Elasticities database collects and models how food demand responds to income and prices around the world. It was published by the International Food Policy Research Institute on Harvard Dataverse in December 2025 and is based on a systematic review and meta-analysis by Roche and colleagues. The meta-sample holds over 13,000 elasticity estimates from 215 peer-reviewed studies published between 1974 and 2022, covering 57 countries, of which 6,572 are income and 6,701 price elasticities, with details of each study's data and methods and country-level sociodemographic indicators. Predicted elasticities give population-weighted average income and price elasticities for nine food groups by world region as of 2021, from meta-regressions, and projected elasticities give income elasticities to 2050 following the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. The tab-separated files are free to download online under custom Dataverse terms. Caveats: estimates inherit the coverage and methods of the source studies, and the projections depend on SSP assumptions. Simulation uses: demand response parameters for food supply shock, price and trade models. Related records: the USDA commodity and food elasticities (data-commodity-and-food-elasticities-p02898) and the EAT-Lancet scenarios (data-eat-lancet-2025-food-system-scenarios) are related inputs.
